item1.justification: The §103 analysis consistently applies Graham/KSR factors (scope and content, differences, PHOSITA level, secondary considerations) for each claim, and §102 anticipation is analyzed element-by-element with specific reference to US-2012302167-A1 disclosures.

item2.justification: Every rejection cites specific claim language (e.g., 'automatic execution of handwriting recognition engine,' 'boot-time initiation') and maps it to specific disclosures in US-2012302167-A1 (e.g., paragraph references, claim 1/2 of the reference, file generation with output data and screen image).

item3.justification: Claims found non-novel at §102 are carried forward as obvious at §103 with the same prior art, and claims 8/10/20 found novel at §102 are then subjected to §103 with additional rationale about boot-time service initiation being a known technique but lacking motivation — no contradictions between stages.

item4.justification: With strictness=0.523 (near neutral) and combination_threshold=0.48, the examiner correctly rejects the bulk of claims strongly but acknowledges weak motivation for boot-time claims (8, 10, 20) with confidence 0.55, yet ultimately rejects all claims — consistent with a moderate examiner who resolves borderline cases against allowance without being lenient.

item5.justification: The final decision to reject all claims follows logically from the accumulated §102 and §103 findings, with explicit weighing distinguishing strong rejections (claims 1-7, 9, 11-19) from weak ones (8, 10, 20) and explaining why even weak §103 grounds suffice for the latter.
